invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Opening run follows the Design Release 2.1 step order and ends on the review page
increments.detail: A trader starting a new notification is carried through the pages in Design Release 2.1's order: the reason for import is asked straight after what is being imported and before commodity details, the CPH number page is no longer a step after roles and addresses (it is reached only from its row there), roles and addresses goes on to the contact address unless everything is already complete, and the contact address always goes on to the review page, which names anything still outstanding. The tests repo's full journey is rewritten as Design Release 2.1's cattle-by-air journey in the new order, because today's cattle-by-road walk follows the old order and would break.

increments.title: A page opened from an overview task returns to the overview when saved
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 sends a trader who opens a page from its task on the overview back to the overview on 'Save and continue', rather than on through the rest of the page's flow section. The service tells such a page by its own journey state, not by a marker in the page address: any save made outside the opening run and outside a change from the review page returns to the overview. Every page the journey chains to today has its own row on the overview, so nothing becomes unreachable. Design Release 2.1 sends a trader who opens a page from its task on the live-animals Overview back to the Overview on 'Save and continue', rather than on through the rest of the section. Today the main import reason runs on to Additional details, Arrival details runs on to Transit countries and Transport details, and the consignment addresses page runs on to the CPH number page. Only the live flow's own fallback changes: no marker is added to the row links or the forms (9 October ruling, c-243).
acceptanceCriteria: Opened from its overview task, 'What are you importing?' goes to the overview on 'Save and continue', not to 'Commodity details'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1588-1602; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-196 to p1-198)

increments.title: 'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader leave most pages for the overview without finishing them, so they can come back later. The backend already stores missing or empty answers. An answer that breaks its own format rule is still refused, because the service cannot store a value that does not fit its field, and consignment details, the CPH number page and the contact address page keep checking their answers before saving.
acceptanceCriteria: On origin of the import, 'What are you importing?', 'Main reason for import', 'Identification details', 'Additional details', 'Arrival details', 'Transit countries', the transporter page, 'Upload documents' and 'Roles and addresses', pressing 'Save and return to overview' with a required answer missing shows no error, saves what was entered and goes to the overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1560-1566, p1-068)
After such a save the page's overview task does not read 'Complete', and reopening the page shows the answers that were entered. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:163-164)

An answer that fails its own format rule, such as an impossible arrival date or a malformed region code, is refused on 'Save and return to overview' with that answer's error, and the page is not saved. (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 10)

On 'Commodity details' and 'Contact address for this consignment', 'Save and return to overview' with a required answer missing shows the page's errors and saves nothing. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162)

In the high-risk plants frontend, 'Save and return to overview' saves what was entered and goes to the Overview without refusing the page for a missing required answer, such as a blank arrival status, date, time or place of landing (repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p5-060, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-117; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-016; c-313)

increments.title: During an amendment, pages end with Save and return, Save and continue and Save and return to overview, and Continue on the amend review is held while anything is incomplete, in animals and plants
increments.detail: While amending, Design Release 2.1 lets the trader save a page and go straight back to the amend review, carry on to the next page, or return to the overview, and it quietly holds Continue on the amend review until every answer is complete and valid. Today a Change link opens a question in change mode and saving always returns to the notification view, and an amendment reaches the declaration only once every task row is fulfilled. After this change each overview-linked page ends with 'Save and return' (to the amend review), 'Save and continue' and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview' while amending; the party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page show the first two only (c-210); question pages keep their usual Back links; and Continue on an incomplete or invalid amend review leaves the trader there with no error summary (c-201). The buttons post the real service's own fields: exit=hub and ?change=1 stay, with no new action field (c-267). The 9 October afternoon ruling makes the same change in the high-risk plants frontend in the same increment: its save actions get the same three amend controls, its pickers the same two buttons, and its amend review holds Continue without an error summary.

Today the tag reads 'Amending' and only the review page offers a 'Cancel amendment' link, under its heading. The 9 October afternoon ruling makes this the one change to the shared status strip itself (claim 40): it adds Cancel amend for status AMEND and changes 'Amending' to 'Amend' in every set at once, live animals, germinal products and plants. notes: Combines the drafts of the manage-notifications, notification-hub areas for this row: they change the same page, record or set-up, so building them apart would repeat it.

Re-distil under the 9 October afternoon ruling: the bar's Cancel amend goes to the cancel confirmation page, not a dialog (claim 19, p1-086). Claim 40 makes this row the one change to the shared strip itself; p3-045 says plants picks it up from that change, but plants keeps its own copy of the shared layout and kit, so the same strip change is made there in this increment, with no other plants work. Pass 2 combines the tag copy (req-1397) and the bar (req-1398): the bar carries the tag. The existing row also carries req-782 (the hub's status line, notification-hub area) and its hub criteria; the combiner keeps req-782 and those criteria here as before. Depends on the cancel-amendment row, whose 'Go back' and wording the bar leads to. The declaration carries no status bar (req-917). The tests repo's reference-strip and cancel-amend specs move from 'Amending' to 'Amend' and find Cancel amend in the bar.

existingRow inc-122 already holds req-782 with the manage-notifications area's Amend bar on every page (req-1397, req-1398). Drafted here so this area covers req-782; the combiner keeps inc-122's id and theme and merges these criteria in.

c-127 (ruled): the control shows on the Overview and goes to the cancel-amendment confirmation page. inc-122 today carries a criterion that 'Cancel amend' on a question page opens a dialog over the page; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-083 and p1-088 keep the confirmation a page and park the pop-up in its own waiting-on-design increment, so the combiner should reword that criterion to the confirmation page.

Decision: req-782 says the plants Overview gets the bar 'with no plants-specific work'. The plants frontend is a separate repo with its own copy of the shared strip (its shared/kit.js has the same AMEND strip entry), so the animals change cannot reach it on its own. I read the requirement as: plants takes the same shared-strip change in its own shared code in this increment (ruling p3-001, p3-002), and nothing on plants' Overview page itself. So plantsfrontend joins this row's repos (ruling p3-007 adds it to the programme); the combiner adds plantsfrontend to the envelope's repos if it is not there.

The germinal Overview inherits the bar from the shared strip once inc-099 copies the Overview; its own criterion is not written here because a germinal amendment needs the germinal set's submit and amend rows.

Theme moved to journey-foundation: this row changes the shared layout, status strip or page titles of every frontend, which the foundation theme owns so the shared change is made once, in an early wave (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 40 for the Amend bar, claim 53 for the titles).

Its dependency on the cancel-amendment row (inc-121) is dropped: the bar's 'Cancel amend' leads to today's cancel-amendment page, which already exists, and inc-121 rewords that page later. Keeping it would make the foundation theme wait on manage-notifications, which itself waits on the foundation. req-2061 (the 'Amend' tag, once, in the shared strip of every set) is added here by the combiner.

increments.title: Page titles on the INS front door and in plants follow the GOV.UK title pattern, including the INS home's 'Dashboard' title
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 uses one browser title pattern on every page. The INS frontend's titles change from '<page title> | Import notification service' to '<page title> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', as the animals frontend's already read. The pattern lives in the INS frontend's shared layout, so one change gives every INS page the new title at once. Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling says this is not the blocked dashboard summary information and goes ahead now, on today's pages. Design Release 2.1 titles the home 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK'. Today the INS home's title reads 'Dashboard | Import notification service'. The page's own title stays 'Dashboard'; only the shared title pattern changes, which the layout area's INS title-pattern row already makes for every INS page. This is a title, not summary information, so Sam's 9 October rulings leave it to go ahead on today's home.
acceptanceCriteria: On the INS frontend, every page's browser title reads the page's title, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - ', such as 'Address book - Import notification service - GOV.UK' (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p4-001; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-086; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-064; conflicts:c-146)

notes: Combines the drafts of the layout-and-sign-in, dashboard-home areas for this row: they change the same page, record or set-up, so building them apart would repeat it.

One thin slice: req-1686 is this area's only buildable change that stands on its own; every other adopted requirement here is already met (exists) and goes to the report. The pattern is one line of the INS frontend's shared layout, so the INS dashboard and address book rows assert it on their own pages rather than change it.

c-146 settles the home's own title as 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK', which this pattern produces from today's 'Dashboard' page title; the ruling (claim 53) calls inc-127 the one ready row left in the ins-dashboard theme. The home's title (req-953) sits in inc-128 today, whose other requirements are blocked; the combiner may move req-953 here so the home's title lands now with the pattern.
The 'Error: ' prefix is kept from today's layout. The tests repo has no INS title assertion today, so the end-to-end proof of the pattern is new.

Combiner: merge into inc-127 ('INS page titles follow the GOV.UK title pattern', req-1686, the layout area's row). req-953 was in inc-128, which is now blocked as summary information; its title is not summary information (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-064 names inc-127 as the ready row in this theme), and inc-127's shared-layout change produces exactly this title, so building it apart would repeat the same set-up.
The home keeps its page title 'Dashboard' from today's copy; nothing else on the home changes in this row.

Theme moved to journey-foundation: this row changes the shared layout, status strip or page titles of every frontend, which the foundation theme owns so the shared change is made once, in an early wave (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 40 for the Amend bar, claim 53 for the titles).

Combines the INS titles (req-1686), the INS home's own title (req-953, moved here from the blocked inc-128 because a title is not summary information) and plants' titles (req-2088), which the ruling builds in the same increment: one title pattern in each frontend's shared layout.
